note: Single source for the human-need vocabulary (D27 Concept, W-66). The intent-slot schema enum, the system prompts, the ontology entity human_need_concept, the Java bundled schema and the grading screen must all list exactly these ids; test_vocabulary.py and the Java tests fail if any of them drifts. Definitions, aliases and asks are proposals awaiting Nate's review (Q-OC-11). Asks are deliberately empty where nobody has reviewed a mapping: a need never picks a device by itself.

decided.cold, hot, stuffy, dark, arriving, leavi: Seed set from D27 (Cowork, 2026-10-14); awaiting Nate (Q-OC-11). stuffy was folded into humid on 2026-10-19 (see humid).
decided.light, nap, wake_up: Added by Nate, 2026-10-16, while grading gold-01: the vocabulary had dark but not the want for light, and bedtime but not nap or wake up. 'bright' and its derivations are synonyms of light, recorded as aliases so one idea has one label (Nate confirmed this on 2026-10-16: one observational concept, different aliases).
decided.humid: Added 2026-10-19 at Nate's direction (replacing the draft word 'damp'): humidity is moisture in the air, often felt as extra warmth. Nate, 2026-10-19 (grading gold-25 and in chat): 'stuffy is a pseudonym for Humid, treat them as the same concept', so stuffy, muggy, stale air and needs air are aliases of humid and stuffy is no longer a concept. 'Damp' is deliberately not an alias: wet surfaces and leaks belong to the leak and freeze flows, never to this need. The asks are Cowork proposals awaiting Nate's review; the server, not the model, chooses any response.

concepts.label: Humid
concepts.definition: The air feels too moist, close or stuffy, which the person often experiences as extra warmth or stale air. Moisture or poor air movement in the air, not a wet surface or a leak: water on a surface is never this need.
examples: It is too humid in here

concepts.label: Dark
concepts.definition: States that it is too dark: a lack of light described as a condition ("it's dark in here", "I can't see"). Wanting light or brightness as the thing asked for is `light`.

relates_to.note: Wording decides: a stated lack is dark, a stated want is light. Both are satisfied by adding light.

concepts.label: Light
concepts.definition: Wants light or more brightness, stated as the thing wanted ("I need more light", "it needs to be brighter"). 'Bright' and every other form of light or bright (brighter, brighten, brightness, lighten, lighting...) are the same observation and are aliases, not separate concepts. The opposite wish (too bright, want less light) is not in the vocabulary yet.

relates_to.note: Wording decides: a stated want is light, a stated lack is dark.

examples: It needs to be brighter in here

concepts.label: Arriving
concepts.definition: The person is arriving, or about to arrive, at the place.
examples: I am on my way in

concepts.label: Leaving
concepts.definition: The person is leaving, or about to leave, the place.

concepts.label: Bedtime
concepts.definition: Going to bed for the night.

relates_to.note: A nap is a short daytime rest.

concepts.label: Nap
concepts.definition: A short rest during the day, not going to bed for the night.

relates_to.note: Bedtime is sleeping for the night.

examples: I'm going to take a nap
I need to lie down for a bit

concepts.label: Wake up
concepts.definition: Waking up or getting up now. A request to be woken at a future time ("wake me at 7") is a schedule, not this need.

concepts.label: TV time
concepts.definition: The person wants to watch television.
